title: Social determinants of emotional well-being
summary: The study examines how gender roles - i.e. social expectations of ‘typically masculine’ or ‘typically feminine’ behaviour - can influence mental health. It analyses whether people who combine both masculine and feminine characteristics are psychologically more flexible and resilient. Another focus is on how well people deal with stressful situations (coping strategies) and whether people with flexible gender roles use more versatile and healthier strategies. To this end, people with and without mental illness are compared in order to better understand which role models and behaviours might possibly act as a risk or protective factor for mental health.
conditions: Mental and behavioural disorders due to multiple drug use and use of other psychoactive substances: Dependence syndrome
Disorders of adult personality and behaviour
